$comment: First-load budgets for the web app. Enforced by src/size-budget.test.ts; reported on
every PR by tools/report-size-budget.mjs. JSON carries no comments, so the reasoning
lives in `why` fields and in apps/web/src/size-budget.test.ts's header.
WHAT IS BUDGETED is the TOTAL first-load payload -- the page shell plus every engine
artifact a user downloads before their first operation can run -- not only per-file
sizes. Three files each growing 4% is a 4% regression that no 10%-per-file budget
notices. So `total` is the binding gate and the per-artifact lines say WHERE it went.
ORIGIN. docs/spikes/0001-wasm-engines.md measured the option-1 payload at 6,502,775
raw / 2,200,580 brotli, 82% of it PDFium, and ROADMAP item 11 records that as 'the
starting point, not a target'. The shipped build has since drifted above it: qpdf is
now built from source against our own vendored zlib and libjpeg-turbo (1,199,200 raw
against the spike's 917,305), the Rust module has grown from 15,266 to 43,072, and
the three glue files the spike listed separately now live inside one worker bundle.
The numbers below are a fresh measurement of what actually ships, not the spike's
table. pdfium.wasm's brotli size is unchanged from the spike to the byte.
TO CHANGE A BUDGET: re-measure, update `measured_brotli` AND `budget_brotli`, and say
why in the commit. An engine pin bump is the expected reason. Raising a budget to make
CI pass without knowing what grew is the thing this file exists to prevent.
WHEN THE TOTAL IS RE-RAISED TO 3%, because this file now contains two decisions that look
opposite. M1 PR B3 refused a raise at 2.6% headroom -- "raising a budget that is not
binding would spend margin nobody needed" -- and the consolidation batch took one at 2.0%.
The discriminator is not the number: it is whether the PAYLOAD grew or the MEASUREMENT
changed. Growth eats the recorded headroom and is supposed to; that is what the margin is
for, and raising it back would be refunding the thing being measured. A measurement that
stops being blind is different -- the payload was always that size, the file was simply
wrong about it -- and leaving the total there would mean this file claiming 3% while
enforcing 2.0%, which is the quiet disagreement it exists to prevent.
The residual cost is stated rather than glossed: the raise hands out 67 KB of room at the
moment the measurement got sharper, which is the moment a gate is most useful tight. What
makes that acceptable is that nothing is unwatched -- every artifact line keeps its own headroom
headroom, and the newly-visible bytes landed on `page-js`, which has one.
RAISED ONCE SO FAR, in M1 PR B2, for merge's write path. Per-artifact budgets are
recomputed only for lines that MOVED -- raising one that did not would be a silent
widening nobody asked for -- and `page` was on an absolute budget rather than a

percentage until spike 0004, when its slack alone came to more than half the
    total's -- see `headroom.why`.
HOW A RECORDING IS HELD TO THE BUILD IT DESCRIBES.
Each artifact records `measured_sha256` beside its sizes, and src/size-budget-drift.ts
turns that into a contradiction the tests can see: same bytes must mean the same
recorded numbers. Identical bytes with a different `measured_brotli` is a FALSE RECORD,
not drift, and there is no tolerance for it.
This exists because the obvious gates do not cover it. Live sizes are checked against
`budget_brotli`, and the recorded lines are checked against each other -- so a recording
that drifts CONSISTENTLY satisfies both. Measured: `engines/burrow-worker.js` was
recorded at 255,535 raw / 45,052 brotli and measured 256,255 / 45,288 on an UNCHANGED
checkout, 236 brotli bytes from a differently-built, gitignored
`bindings/burrow-wasm/pkg/`. Nothing failed. M1 PR A corrected the number; a corrected
number is not a control, because the next drift is silent in exactly the same way.
`not_byte_reproducible` is the one window this cannot close exactly, and it is declared
rather than implied: those artifacts legitimately differ per machine, so they get a
`drift_tolerance` bound instead of an equality. Every entry needs a reason. An artifact
whose bytes change WITHOUT being on that list fails -- an engine moving underneath us
should not be waved through as 'probably the toolchain'. Two of the three entries were
predicted; `engines/qpdf.wasm` was NOT, and got there by failing CI and naming itself,
which is the check working rather than the check being wrong.
THE PAGE WAS NOT ON THAT LIST, DELIBERATELY, AND IT TOOK TWO GOES -- AND IN M1 PR B3 IT
WENT ON ANYWAY. The argument below is still the right argument and it lost to a fact: the
island's minified bytes differ between architectures. The `not_byte_reproducible` entry for
`page` records what was measured, what was tried first, and what it costs. Read them
together; the paragraph below is kept rather than rewritten because the reasoning did not
stop being sound.
engine by its content-hashed URL (ADR 0014), so any engine rebuild changes index.html --
CI reported `qpdf.wasm` and `page` together for that one cause. Exempting `page` would
have meant not checking the line the design system lives on because of something
belonging to a different line.
So each artifact records TWO digests: the raw bytes, and the bytes with generated engine
hashes replaced by a fixed token. Three cases, distinguished rather than collapsed:
raw match              -> exact size equality. Nothing changed, so no tolerance.
normalised match only  -> only the quoted engine hashes differ. The artifact's own
content is unchanged, but its SIZE may wobble, because two
16-hex tokens do not compress identically. A tight absolute
bound (64 bytes), not a percentage: 2% of the page is 433
bytes and a real CSS regression could hide under that.
normalised differs     -> a real change. Must be on not_byte_reproducible or it fails.
The middle case exists because collapsing it into the first was a bug, and CI caught it:
the check reported `page: the bytes are IDENTICAL to the recording, but measured_brotli
says 21652 and the build is 21650`. The bytes were not identical. The message was the
part that was false, and a check that misdescribes what it found is worse than one that
finds nothing.
Shortening that list is the real fix and it means making `pkg/` reproducible, which is a
build change nobody has made yet.

why: Per-artifact headroom is loose (25%) because those lines are diagnostic: they say
which file moved. Total headroom is tight (10%, about 46 KB) because that line is the
gate. Both numbers were re-derived when PDFium left the payload; the paragraphs below
record what each was, what it is, and why it moved.
THE ASYMMETRY USED TO CARRY A CLAIM THAT IS NOW MEASURED FALSE. It said the total
'binds first in every case that matters -- 10% of pdfium alone is 8.5% of the total, so
a single artifact cannot reach its own ceiling without the total having failed long
before'. That holds for a LARGE artifact and not for a small one. M1's split bridge grew
`burrow_wasm_bg.wasm` by 65.7%, which blew its own ceiling while moving the total by
1.24% -- because 10% of a 36 KiB artifact is 0.15% of a 2.3 MiB payload.
So a per-artifact line CAN fire alone, and when it does it is doing the job the block
describes: saying which file moved. What it is not is a second gate, and raising one
must not be read as spending total margin -- the total is recorded separately and was
`page` is the exception and is recorded as such rather than left to look like 10%:
its budget is an ABSOLUTE 50 KiB, 58x its measurement. The reason is on that line.

THE TOTAL'S HEADROOM IS 10%, RAISED FROM 3% WHEN THE PAYLOAD FELL BY 80.7%. Not because the margin was wrong before, but because a percentage of 2.4 MB and a percentage of 462 KB are different instruments. 3% of the new total is 13,877 bytes --- inside the noise of a routine dependency bump --- so a 3% gate would fire on churn and be raised by whoever was holding it, which is how a budget becomes a formality. 10% is 46,256 bytes: large enough that an ordinary bump does not reach it, small enough that a real regression does.

AND `page` IS NO LONGER AN EXCEPTION -- IT IS ON THE PER-ARTIFACT RULE, 25%, like every other line, and `headroom.page` records that rate rather than a different one. (It was recorded as 0.10 in the first draft of this change while the line itself was derived at 1.25x, so the file disagreed with itself about a number nothing reads -- `size-budget.test.ts` consumes only `total` and `per_artifact`. An unenforced claim is the one that rots.) Its absolute 50 KiB was set when the line measured 881 bytes and was 58x it; the self-hosted typeface then took it to 22,550, and the absolute quietly became 2.3x. At the old total that was affordable. At the new one its slack alone (28,650 bytes) is more than half the entire total's headroom, so the line could absorb a regression the total was supposed to catch and report nothing. It is on the same per-artifact rule as everything else now, which is what the rest of this block already claimed the file did.

PER-ARTIFACT HEADROOM WIDENED 10% -> 25%, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM. The total only catches what the lines miss if it is the TIGHTER of the two: the `catches a regression split across three files` test looks for a uniform growth that every per-artifact line passes and the total still refuses, and no such growth exists when both numbers are equal. Setting the total to 10% therefore forced the lines wider, not narrower. They lose nothing by it --- they are diagnostic, they say WHICH file moved, and the total fires first for almost any real growth anyway: 25% of qpdf.wasm alone is 18% of the payload, well past the total's 10%.

engines/qpdf.wasm.why: Built from source at the pinned version against our vendored zlib and libjpeg-turbo, so it moves with a pin bump or a build-flag change. M1 PR B2 MOVED IT BY +53,456 BROTLI (265,985 -> 319,441), and that is the single largest deliberate increase this payload has taken. The cause is qpdf's QPDFWriter and its dependencies, pulled in by adding seven entry points to EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS so merge can produce bytes on the web. ADR 0017 chose qpdf over PDFium for fidelity -- PDFium loses outlines, attachments and the /AcroForm, and the last of those silently leaves a form field that is no longer a field. PDFium already exports everything a merge needs, so choosing it would have cost ZERO bytes. This line is the price of that decision, and it is recorded here so the trade stays visible rather than becoming a number nobody can explain. M1's rotate bridge moved it +3,287 brotli (319,441 -> 322,728) by adding six `qpdf_oh_*` functions to EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS -- small beside merge's +53,456, because those seven entry points pulled in QPDFWriter and these six pull in accessors qpdf already links. It is now 70.8% of the whole payload (327,629 of 462,562), where it was 13.7%. Nothing about the artifact changed; everything about its share did.

engines/burrow-worker.js.why: The one bundle: prelude, bridge, the qpdf Emscripten glue, wasm-bindgen glue, worker main. It carried BOTH glue files until spike 0004 took PDFium out of the payload. This is the line our own worker code moves, so it is the one worth watching on an ordinary PR. M1 PR B2 added +2,628 -- the write path's nine bridge functions and the wasm-bindgen glue for the merge entry point. M1 PR B3 took it DOWN by 13 (48,092 -> 48,079): unwrapping `InputFailed` for the reply's limit detail added code, and one `innermost` helper replacing three ad-hoc unwraps took back slightly more than it cost. M1's consolidation batch added +1,125 for the pre-flight budget call and the Reply it drains. And +635 for the start-up progress message the stall bound reads (ADR 0018). M1's rotate bridge moved it +1,924 brotli: six `__burrow_qpdf_oh_*` forwarders, the `rotate` and `page_rotations` dispatch arms, and the `rotations` line in `drainReply`. ADR 0022 added +14: the `OutputRejected` kind crossing the reply boundary. RAISED IN M1's SPLIT BRIDGE, from 57,483 to 62,630, and NOT because it is close to failing: 56,936 against 57,483 is 1% of headroom where this file records 10%, and the across-the-board regression test said so first -- at +4% the worker alone would have exceeded its own budget, which would have made that test prove nothing rather than prove the total binds. The +3,591 is the multi-output protocol (ADR 0023): the part and progress messages, the cut validation, and the refusal helper the split arm shares with the others. A per-artifact budget that has drifted to 1% has stopped being diagnostic and started being a second gate, which is the thing the headroom block says it is not. SPIKE 0004 HALVED IT: 56,936 -> 33,830 brotli (both endpoints are the values recorded in this file; an earlier draft of this sentence quoted a pair that matched neither), because PDFium's 164 KB of Emscripten glue was concatenated into this bundle. The budget is recomputed from the new measurement rather than left at a number set for a bundle twice this size --- a 10% headroom over a figure that no longer describes the file is not headroom, it is a gate that cannot fire.

engines/burrow_wasm_bg.wasm.why: The Rust binding: every entry point, the reply shape, and now the PRUNING POLICY and the PDF tokeniser, which split's bridge makes reachable from the web for the first time. RAISED IN M1's SPLIT BRIDGE, from 37,276 to 61,775, and the growth is the feature rather than a regression: 33,887 -> 56,159 brotli, +65.7%, of which the policy (crate::prune) and the lexer (crate::pdfsyntax) are the bulk -- roughly 1,300 lines of Rust that did not previously link into this module because no web operation reached them. The session type and the split entry point are the rest. It is a DIAGNOSTIC line, not the gate: the total is what binds, and it did not move past its budget. But this artifact is the first to blow its own ceiling while the total held, which falsifies a claim the headroom block used to make -- see there.

engines/control.txt.why: A fixed 78-byte literal fetched at init to prove an allowlisted request succeeds (ADR 0014). It has no reason to change; if it does, that is worth a question.

page.why: The heaviest landing route's markup, stylesheets and fonts, pooled -- Vite splits and names those chunks at its own discretion, so a per-file budget here would fail on a rename. SCRIPTS ARE NOT ON THIS LINE ANY MORE; they are on `page-js`, for the reason recorded there and in tools/first-load.mjs. That split is what lets this line keep the EXACT digest check: it was briefly on not_byte_reproducible with a 2% bound, about 600 bytes, which is enough to hide a CSS regression -- and the thing it was tolerating belonged entirely to the JavaScript. ON THE PER-ARTIFACT RULE (25%), not an absolute. It was an absolute 50 KiB until spike 0004; see `headroom.why` for why that stopped working when the payload fell by 80.7%. The route is the heaviest one, not the home page: people arrive from a search for "merge pdf" and land on /merge-pdf. `measured_route` records which one that was, and the test fails if the build disagrees. M1 PR A moved this line from 881 to 21,652 brotli, and almost all of that is one file: the self-hosted typeface, 18,524 of it. apps/web/fonts.toml records what the face is and what the alternatives cost (brotli: 47,804 unsubsetted, 31,620 subsetted with the full weight axis, 18,524 with the axis clipped to the 400-700 the design uses). The font is only in this measurement because BaseLayout preloads it: tools/first-load.mjs scans the markup and does not follow url(...) inside CSS, so a face referenced only from @font-face would be a real download this budget could not see. src/styles/tokens.test.ts fails if any @font-face here has no matching preload. M1's ROTATE PAGE OVERTOOK MERGE AS THE HEAVIEST ROUTE, by 500 brotli bytes (2,350,467 against 2,349,967) -- the two pages are within a rounding error of each other and rotate's prose is slightly longer. The test caught the change rather than letting the line quietly start meaning a different page, which is exactly what `measured_route` is for. Re-measured against /rotate-pdf, and the budget was then still an absolute 50 KiB. ADR 0022 took it DOWN by 11, which is a compression effect rather than a saving: the page markup did not change. M1's SPLIT PAGE OVERTOOK ROTATE AS THE HEAVIEST ROUTE, by 701 brotli bytes (2,392,045 against 2,391,344) --- the five routes now sit within 2,850 bytes of each other, so which one is heaviest is decided by prose length and will keep changing. The test reported the change rather than letting the line quietly start meaning a different page, which is what `measured_route` is for. +352 brotli on this line is /split-pdf's markup: it carries ADR 0019 §4's three consequences, which are longer than rotate's prose. THE RANGE AND THE EVERY-PAGE PRESET added +109 on `page` and +441 on `page-js`. They are not a convenience: without them, splitting a forty-page document into single pages needed 39 cut points typed by hand (145 characters) and a five-hundred-page one needed 499 (2,385), so one of the two things people most want from a splitter was unreachable rather than tedious. /reorder-pdf does the equivalent in five characters. SPIKE 0004 TOOK PDFIUM OUT OF THE WEB PAYLOAD, and every line here is re-measured against that build. This is the first re-recording in this file that is a REDUCTION rather than growth, so the usual rule --- recompute only the lines that moved --- does not apply: removing an artifact changes what the total means, so all of it is measured again rather than arithmetic being done on the old numbers.

page-js.why: Every bundled script the heaviest landing route needs: the island that mounts the merge tool, and the Svelte runtime it imports. IT IS ITS OWN LINE BECAUSE IT IS THE ONLY PART OF THE PAGE THAT IS NOT BYTE-REPRODUCIBLE. Measured, not assumed: M1's consolidation batch pushed a per-file digest breakdown to CI, and against this aarch64 recording the x86_64 build reported identical digests for the markup, both stylesheets and the font, and a different one for the island chunk alone -- the bundler's native binary mangles identifiers differently. Pooled with the rest, that cost the whole page line its exact check. THE RUNTIME CHUNK WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW, and it is 31 KB raw of the 52 KB here. `firstLoad` derived the payload from the markup alone and did not follow a script's own `import`s, so a third of the page's real JavaScript was a download nothing watched -- found while splitting this line, not by anything failing. The budget is the usual 10% per-artifact headroom on a fresh measurement. M1's consolidation batch added +192 for the "getting the engine ready" line the page now shows while the engines load (ADR 0018). ADR 0022 added +225: `tool-delivery.ts` -- one generation-and-handout path shared by the three islands instead of three copies (#69) -- and an `OutputRejected` sentence on each tool page, which #61's discharge needs because the generic "your file is fine, try again" is false on exactly the document that refusal is about. M1's SPLIT PAGE added +455 brotli: the fourth island, plus `split-cuts.ts` and `split-messages.ts`, minus what the bundler now shares across four islands rather than three. The island itself is larger than reorder's --- it carries a progress readout and a list of results rather than one link --- and most of it lands in the chunk this line measures. RAISED HERE, from 22,730 to 24,289, and NOT because it is close to failing: 22,081 against 22,730 is 2.9% of headroom where this file records 10%, and the across-the-board regression test said so first --- at +4% this line alone would have exceeded its own budget, which would have made that test prove nothing rather than prove the total binds. Exactly the reasoning the split BRIDGE's raise of `burrow-worker.js` records, one line along: a per-artifact budget that has drifted to single-figure headroom has stopped being diagnostic and started being a second gate, which the headroom block says it is not. The TOTAL is not raised and is recorded separately. THE RANGE AND THE EVERY-PAGE PRESET added +109 on `page` and +441 on `page-js`. They are not a convenience: without them, splitting a forty-page document into single pages needed 39 cut points typed by hand (145 characters) and a five-hundred-page one needed 499 (2,385), so one of the two things people most want from a splitter was unreachable rather than tedious. /reorder-pdf does the equivalent in five characters.

total.why: The binding gate. Everything a user downloads before their first operation runs. RAISED IN M1 PR B2, from 2,299,796 to 2,383,361, and this is the first raise. The payload grew 60,124 brotli bytes because merge needs an engine that can WRITE: qpdf's QPDFWriter (+53,456), the Rust entry point (+4,044) and the bridge (+2,628). The raise restores the recorded 3% headroom rather than inventing a new margin, and the alternative was measured rather than assumed -- PDFium can merge with zero added bytes and loses outlines, attachments and working form fields (ADR 0017). A budget raised without knowing what grew has stopped being a budget; this one names every line that moved and why. M1 PR B3 moved it +8,206, to 2,322,444, and NOT by shipping more engine: the page line changed which route it measures, from the home page to /merge-pdf, which is the heaviest route and the one people actually land on. The budget is NOT raised for it -- 2,383,361 still leaves 2.6% of headroom against the recorded 3%, and raising a budget that is not binding would spend margin nobody needed. RAISED AGAIN IN M1's CONSOLIDATION BATCH, from 2,383,361 to 2,403,482, and this raise is unlike the last one: THE PAYLOAD DID NOT GROW. The measurement stopped being blind. `firstLoad` never followed a script's own `import`s, so the Svelte runtime the island pulls in -- 31,063 raw, 11,034 brotli -- was a real download no budget line could see. Counting it moved the total by exactly that. The raise restores the recorded 3% headroom rather than inventing a margin; refusing to raise it would have left the file claiming 3% and enforcing 2.1%, which is the kind of quiet disagreement this file exists to prevent. The pre-flight budget check (#51) added 2,130 on top of that: 1,005 in the Rust module and 1,125 in the worker bundle. Within the budget above; not raised for it. M1's ROTATE PAGE added the second tool page and its island: the total moved to 2350467, which is within the budget above and does not raise it. The page line now measures /rotate-pdf rather than /merge-pdf -- it overtook merge by 500 bytes, which the heaviest-route test reported rather than absorbing. M1's REORDER BRIDGE moved it to 2,356,369, +5,522 against the recording, and every byte is named: the Rust module +2,749 brotli for the `reorder` entry point and three bridge methods; qpdf.wasm +1,561 for four more exported C functions (qpdf_remove_page, qpdf_add_page_at, qpdf_oh_get_object_id, qpdf_oh_get_generation); the worker bundle +1,073 for the protocol branch and its validation; page-js +141 for the conformance driver's `reverseEveryPage`. The budget is NOT raised: 2,403,482 leaves 2.0% of headroom against the recorded 3%, which is the margin narrowing rather than a ceiling being hit. M1's REORDER PAGE moved it to 2,356,831, +462, and the heaviest route did NOT change: `/rotate-pdf` stays the measured one at 2,356,831 with `/reorder-pdf` 1,475 behind it. The +462 is entirely `page-js` -- a third island changes how the bundler splits the shared chunk the measured route pulls in; the reorder island's own code is on a route this line does not measure. Not raised: 2,403,482 leaves 2.0%. M1's SPLIT BRIDGE moved it to 2,389,341, +29,345 against the recording, and every byte is named: the Rust module +22,272 brotli, which is the pruning policy and the PDF tokeniser linking into the web module for the first time; the worker bundle +3,591 for the multi-output protocol (ADR 0023) and its cut validation; qpdf.wasm +3,340 for ten more exported C functions, the object-surgery calls pruning needs; page-js +147. THE BUDGET IS NOT RAISED, and the number that matters is the headroom rather than the verdict: 2,403,482 leaves 14,141 bytes, which is 0.59% against the 3% this file records as the margin. The gate holds and the margin does not, and those are different sentences. The next change of any size will need either a smaller binding or a decision about the total, and pretending otherwise by raising it here would spend the margin quietly -- which is the thing this file exists to stop. M1's SPLIT PAGE moved it to 2,390,148, +807 against the recording, and both lines that moved are named above: +352 on `page` and +455 on `page-js`. THE BUDGET IS NOT RAISED --- 2,403,482 leaves 13,334 bytes, 0.55% against the 3% this file records. The margin is still the thing that is not holding, and spike 0004 is the decision that answers it rather than a raise: PDFium is 79.7% of this payload and the web calls into it from one place. WHAT IS *NOT* RECORDED HERE, deliberately: the live build on this machine measures 2,392,045, about 1,897 bytes above the sum above, entirely from `burrow-worker.js` and `burrow_wasm_bg.wasm`. Those two are on `not_byte_reproducible` because they are built from a gitignored `pkg/` that differs per machine, and no Rust changed in this pull request --- so re-recording them would bake one machine's toolchain into the file and attribute 1,897 bytes to a page that did not cost them. They keep the values they were recorded with, and `drift_tolerance` is what covers the difference. The range and the every-page preset took the recording to 2,390,698. Still NOT RAISED: 2,403,482 leaves 12,784 bytes. SPIKE 0004: PDFium leaves the web payload and the total falls 2,390,698 -> 462,146 brotli, **-80.7%**, which is the largest single change this file has ever recorded and the first downward one. THE BUDGET IS DELIBERATELY NOT LOWERED TO MATCH. Every raise in this file restored a stated margin after a NAMED increase; there is no equivalent ritual for a fall, and lowering it here would decide by accident what the ceiling means now that the payload is a fifth of it. That is a decision to take deliberately, with `compress` --- the last M1 operation, and the one that may want engines nothing here ships --- in front of whoever takes it. Headroom is 1,941,336 bytes, 420% of the payload. LOWERED HERE, 2,403,482 -> 508,361, at 10% over the new total. Left at 2,403,482 the total stopped being a gate at all --- `catches a regression split across three files` measured it: a 4% rise on EVERY artifact came to 480,631 against a 2,403,482 ceiling, so the payload could have quadrupled in silence. That test is the reason this number moved, and it moved once a person decided what the ceiling should mean rather than as a consequence of the payload shrinking. COMPRESS IS EXPECTED TO RAISE IT, and this sentence exists so that raise arrives as a decision with numbers rather than as a surprise: it is the last M1 operation and it may want engines nothing here ships. `hb-subset` is a separate HarfBuzz target PDFium does not build --- HarfBuzz itself is already linked inside PDFium (ADR 0010), the SUBSETTER is not --- and `jbig2enc` is not pinned, not licence-audited and needs an ADR under the allowlist rule before its size matters. NEITHER HAS A MEASURED WASM SIZE, here or in spike 0004, and this file does not invent one. Whoever adds either measures it first and raises this line by what they measured. RE-RECORDED AT 462,562 / 508,818 BEFORE THE PR OPENED, +416 brotli on the -80.7% figure above, and the delta is named rather than smoothed: +414 is `burrow-worker.js` and +4 is `page`, all of it COMMENT TEXT --- the worker bundle is concatenated rather than minified, so the corrections two reviews asked for (stale PDFium prose, five wrong numbers, a bullet that generalised a PDFium constraint onto qpdf) are bytes a person downloads. The 10% rule is re-derived against the new measurement rather than the old one, so the headroom is 46,256 bytes exactly. Worth stating because it is the smallest kind of growth this file records and the easiest to let pass as rounding: prose in a shipped file is payload.

not_byte_reproducible.engines/burrow_wasm_bg.wasm: wasm-pack output. bindings/burrow-wasm/pkg/ is gitignored and rebuilt per machine, so the bytes depend on the local Rust and wasm-bindgen versions rather than on anything committed.
not_byte_reproducible.engines/burrow-worker.js: Concatenates pkg/burrow_wasm.js, so it inherits the line above. THIS IS THE ONE THAT DRIFTED: recorded at 45,052 brotli and measuring 45,288 on an unchanged checkout, 236 bytes from a differently-built pkg/, with nothing failing.
not_byte_reproducible.engines/qpdf.wasm: Built from source by engines/build-wasm.sh rather than fetched, and OBSERVED to differ between a local build and CI -- which is how it got onto this list: the check failed and named it. The cause is not established. emsdk is pinned (ADR 0004), so a reproducible Emscripten build is plausible and the usual culprit is absolute paths baked in by the compiler; nobody has looked. Until someone does, this is a bound rather than a claim. pdfium.wasm is NOT here: it is a prebuilt vendored artifact and its bytes match.
not_byte_reproducible.page-js: The bundler's minified output differs between architectures. Measured three times in CI against this recording: two builds on the SAME machine are byte-identical, and the x86_64 build assigns mangled identifiers differently from this aarch64 one -- `f as Ie` here, `f as xe` there. This is the whole reason scripts have their own budget line: pooled with the markup and stylesheets it took THOSE off the exact check too. Restoring an exact check here needs a reproducible bundle, which means pinning the bundler's output across architectures or recording on the architecture CI uses. Neither has been attempted.
